03_marg367: ISIDORE. Adding sins to sins, he despairs and does not believe that he can obtain pardon; which is the blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, which is not forgiven in this world nor in the world to come, because he thinks that God either will not forgive or cannot, as if he either could not do all things or grudged salvation.
03_marg368: Every one, therefore, that, etc. STRABO. Because from the trembling of my body and the agitation of my maddened mind, whoever finds me will know me guilty of death.
03_marg369: You will not die soon, as you wish, as a remedy for your torment; but it will be punished, impersonally, that is, punishment will be taken of you sevenfold, because you will live in torment until the seventh generation, in which you will be killed by Lamech. So everyone who kills (understand) will free you from that torment of a bad conscience. This sense appears more plainly according to the Seventy: “Everyone who kills Cain will pay off seven vengeances,” that is, whoever kills you in the seventh generation will release you by death from the torment, you who are to be kept alive until that time only for punishment; which punishment would soon be ended if you were soon killed. So whoever punished the Jews with visible death would take away from them the seven vengeances to which they are bound for the guilt of killing Christ, because he would lighten their miseries and scatterings which they suffer.
03_marg370: The Seventy: “He will pay off seven vengeances.” Aquila: “sevenfold.” Symmachus: “seven times.” Theodotion renders it “by a week”; in which it is signified that he will be punished long and thoroughly, so that no one should dare to repeat murder.
03_marg371: “He who kills Cain shall be punished sevenfold.” If anyone kills you, he shall be punished sevenfold, that is, he shall be punished with the heaviest vengeance; a man ought not to kill him whose life God kept, either for his punishment or for the correction of others.
03_marg372: “But whosoever shall kill Cain.” It is to be read by ellipsis: “whosoever shall kill Cain,” a break here, then is to be joined: “it shall be punished sevenfold,” not Cain nor the killer, because it is put impersonally; so that we have the same sense as the words of the Seventy translators contain, namely, “he will pay off seven vengeances.” Historically, he was to live in scattering until seven generations; which punishment would at once have been paid off had he been killed then. So whoever punished the Jews with visible death would take away the seven vengeances to which they are bound for the death of Christ; for he would lighten their miseries and scattering, which they suffer in this time, which rolls on in sevens; and that is fulfilled: “Scatter them by thy power.”
03_marg373: What Aquila put, “sevenfold,” and Symmachus, “a week,” or “the seventh shall avenge,” our elders so understood, that Cain was killed by Lamech in the seventh generation. Others, because seven is a full and perfect number, so say that whoever kills Cain will free him from great punishment and every passing torment. Others suppose various things about seven sins of Cain. The first sin, they say, is that he did not divide rightly; the second, that he envied his brother; the third, that he acted craftily, saying, “Let us go into the field”; the fourth, that he killed; the fifth, that he shamelessly denied it; the sixth, that he condemned himself: “My iniquity is greater than that I may deserve pardon”; the seventh, that even when condemned he did not do penance. Hence they say he was put off by God until the seventh generation, so that at least, driven by evils, he might do penance and deserve to be absolved.
03_marg374: And the Lord set a mark, etc. ISIDORE. Though all the nations conquered by the Romans passed into their rites, the Jewish nation, whether under heathen or under Christian kings, has not given up the sign of circumcision and fleshly observance by which it is distinguished from the other nations; and whoever finds them in his kingdom with this sign does not kill them, that is, does not bring it about that they are not Jews, set apart from all by their own sign. But whoever of them has passed over to Christ is no longer found Cain, nor goes out from the face of the Lord, nor dwells in the land of Naid, which is interpreted “commotion,” or unstable and wavering and of uncertain seat; which all suffer who go out from the face of the Lord, that is, from the mercy of his love, and dwell in fleshly disturbance, over against Eden, which is interpreted “feasting,” where paradise was planted.
03_marg375: JEROME. The Seventy: “He dwelt in the land of Naid.” In the Hebrew it is called Nod, that is, unstable and wavering and of uncertain seat. It is not a land of Naid, as our common people think; but the Lord’s sentence is fulfilled while he wanders here and there, a vagabond and fugitive.

03_marg376: And Cain knew, etc. ISIDORE. Figuratively, the offspring of the wicked, seeking its foundation in the very beginning of the world, built a city in this life, which it called Henoch, which is interpreted “dedication,” because they dedicate themselves in the beginnings, while they plant the root of the heart in this life, which comes first, so as to flourish here as they wish and wither from the glory to come. But Abraham dwelt in huts, because the saints know themselves to be guests and pilgrims, looking for a city that hath foundations, whose builder is God.
03_marg377: And he built, etc. AUGUSTINE. It is asked with what helpers he built it, if there were no more men than Scripture says. But it is to be known that there were many more then, because by living long they could beget more; nor is it a wonder, since the children of Israel are read to have so multiplied in four hundred years that their army could not be counted.
03_marg378: And Henoch, etc. JEROME. Not from all these are sure mysteries carved out; nor would they be found unless certain roots of history were first laid down; nor would you gather fruit from the branches of trees unless you had first planted the trunks.
03_marg379: It is to be noted that the generations from Adam through Cain end in eleven, in which transgression is marked. For Lamech is the seventh, to whom three sons and one daughter are added so that eleven is filled, by which sin is signified; for the generation is closed by a woman too, who was the beginning of sin, through which the pleasure of the flesh, which resists the spirit. Whence she is called Noema, that is, pleasure. In this line Lamech first, against custom and against nature, committed adultery by bigamy.

03_marg380: And Ada brought forth Jabel, etc. JEROME. From bigamy is born Jabel, dwelling in tents, which, being changeable, figure the instability of those who are carried about with every wind of doctrine. Jubal too is born, who was the inventor of music, of which it is said that through tuneful music it tempts the ears; which belongs to the pleasure of the ears. Tubalcain is born, who by works of brass invited the desire of the eyes, and by the smith’s art stirred up the cruelty of wars; by whose sister, who is called Noema, that is, pleasure, the desire of the flesh is marked. It is to be noted that these are understood, by figurative speech, partly through the meanings of the names, as Henoch and Noema; partly through the actions of men opposed to good ways, as Jabel, Jubal and Tubalcain.

03_marg383: RABANUS. The Hebrews say that Lamech, from living long, came into dimness of the eyes and had a young man as guide and director of his way. So, while hunting, he aimed an arrow where the young man showed him, and by chance killed Cain, hiding among the shrubs. And this is what he says: “I have slain a man to my wounding,” that is, by the wound which I inflicted I killed not a beast but a man. Whence, kindled with rage, I killed the young man too.
03_marg384: “I have slain a man,” etc., that is, Cain, “to my wounding,” because for him I shall be wounded, that is, killed; “and a stripling to my bruising,” because for him too I shall be condemned.

03_marg385: Sevenfold vengeance shall be taken, etc. ALLEGORICALLY. ALCUIN. The sin of Lamech (which is interpreted “humbled”) signifies the casting-down of the human race, which fell when Adam transgressed and could not rise by the law or circumcision or by its own justice, until after seventy-seven generations, according to Luke, Christ, coming into the world, blotted out sin by the shedding of his blood. Whence: “I say not to thee, till seven times; but till seventy times seven times”; that is, the Jew is to be received after seventy-seven vengeances, if he comes to his senses and seeks Christ’s pardon.
03_marg386: Seven signifies the whole; by which, eleven being multiplied, seventy-seven is made, in which transgression of every kind is marked; which yet in the gospel is commanded to be forgiven the penitent.
03_marg387: They say that from Adam to Christ there are seventy-seven generations, according to Luke. So as the sin of Cain was released in the seventh generation (for God will not judge twice for the same thing, and he who has received his punishment once in his life will not suffer in death the same torments he suffered in life), so too Lamech, that is, the sin of the whole world, will be released by the coming of Christ. A certain Hebrew told me that seventy-seven souls came forth from Lamech, all of whom perished in the flood.
03_interl448: “setting,” who rose up in the place of the one killed
03_marg388: Adam also knew … again, etc. By Seth, who is interpreted “resurrection,” is marked the life of Christ from the dead, which is signified in the mother’s words: “The Lord hath given me another seed”; as if the Church should say: I who bore mourning for the dead rejoice over the one raised up.
03_interl453: confessing God the Creator and the restorer of life
03_marg389: Whom he called, etc. Enos is interpreted “man,” who began to call upon the name of the Lord; because through the death of Christ, which Abel signified, and through the resurrection, which Seth signifies, man is made, confessing the Lord, the Creator and restorer of the life that was lost.
03_marg390: “Whom he called Enos.” Enos is interpreted “man,” who began to call upon the name of the Lord. As Adam is interpreted “man,” so also Enos, according to the Hebrew truth, “man” or “husband”; and fittingly, because he had this name, it was said that the calling upon the name of the Lord began then; although very many of the Hebrews think that then for the first time idols were made in the name of the Lord and in his likeness.
03_interl456: because he was made in the brightness of contemplation
03_marg391: Adam was made to the likeness of God, the others to the likeness of Adam; and it is as it were a conclusion from what goes before, with a summing-up: “In the day that God created man.” For he was created in the day, because he was set in the brightness of divine contemplation. “To the likeness of God,” because he gave him reason, by which, understanding, he should discern good and evil, love what he understood, and not hand over to forgetfulness what he loved; and in this he would keep the likeness of God. But after he blotted out this likeness by disobedience, made earthly, he begot earthly ones. Whence: “Such as is the earthly, such also are the earthly.”
03_interl458: because this was done in both sexes
03_interl459: that is, man, because he was taken from the ground
03_interl460: he returns to the order of weaving the genealogy
03_marg392: And Adam lived, etc. JEROME. It is to be known that up to the flood, where in our copies someone is said to have begotten at two hundred and some years, the Hebrew has a hundred years and the rest that follow.
03_marg393: And begot, etc. As if: this one too, who was put in place of the just Abel and by the meaning of his name signifies Christ, bore the image of the earthly. But all bear the image of the earthly man before the heavenly, although many before the coming of Christ had, through faith, the same grace by which Christians are saved.
03_marg394: They say that after the death of Abel Adam vowed that he would no more know his wife nor beget a son. But at God’s command he broke the vow, so that the Son of God should be born of him and man be redeemed; for he ought not to be born from the stock of Cain. Whence no one is read to have been begotten before Seth; but after him it is said that he begot sons and daughters.
03_marg395: This reckoning of the genealogies spreads as it were branches of histories, from which in their own places the fruits of mysteries are gathered. And it is to be noted that in the generation of Seth no woman is set down by name, as in the generation of Cain. For it belongs to the just to do all things manfully, to take up nothing womanish, nothing frail. For this generation goes on by ten up to Noe, in whom the fulfilling of the commandments is marked, as by eleven in the generation of Cain, transgression.
03_marg396: In the generation of the unjust Henoch is put first, which is interpreted “dedication,” because the reprobate fix the root of their hope in the present life and wither from love of the unfading inheritance; of whom it is said: “I have seen a fool with a strong root, and I cursed his beauty immediately.” In the generation of the just Henoch is put seventh from Adam, because these do not seek an abiding city here, but stretch their expectation to the end of time, which is closed by the sevenfold turning, when the eighth, eternity, shall have followed. Whence this Henoch, who is put seventh and was translated because he pleased God, signifies the seventh rest, to which whoever clings to God perseveringly is carried without delay after this life. The meaning of the names of this generation, too, marks the same thing. Adam is interpreted “man” or “red earth”; Seth, “setting” or “resurrection”; Enos, “man”; Cainan, “lamentation”; Malaleel, “praising God”; Jared, “strengthened”; Henoch, “dedication”; Mathusala, “the sending-forth of death”; Lamech, “humbled”; Noe, “rest.” So man, coming forth from the earth, rising again from sins, will be a man calling upon God and weeping for his former sins; and so, praising God, strengthened by the Spirit of God, he is dedicated to eternal life; and, victor over death, subject to God, he possesses everlasting rest, which Noe signifies, who is interpreted “rest” and is counted in the tenth place, because the kingdom of heaven is possessed through the fulfilling of the commandments.
03_marg397: And he walked with God, etc. ISIDORE. Henoch, seventh from Adam, pleasing God, who was also translated, signifies the seventh rest, to which is carried he who is formed as on the sixth day, that is, in the sixth age of the world, through the coming of Christ; and when six thousand years are past, the judgment made, and heaven and earth renewed, the saints will be carried into eternal life. But that through Seth, from Adam to Noe, the number ten is suggested, the fulfilment of the commandments in the Church in works is figured; to which number, if the two sons of Noe are added, the middle one being rejected, twelve is completed, which is held notable in the number of the patriarchs and apostles because of the parts of seven multiplied one by the other; for three fours make it.
03_marg398: Henoch is kept from death for so long a time, in which it is shown that man would always have lived had he not sinned.
03_marg399: And Mathusala lived, etc. It is asked how Mathusala, by the reckoning of the years, could live after the flood, since all perished except those who went into the ark. But the faultiness of the copies gave rise to this question; for not only is it found otherwise in the Hebrew, but also in the Seventy translation, in a few copies, Mathusala is found to have died seven years before the flood.
03_marg400: That the years of Mathusala are counted beyond the flood according to the Seventy is because he signifies Christ, whose life feels no age; so that in the elders too he should seem not to have felt the flood.
03_marg401: And all the days … were, etc. JEROME. “And all the days of Mathusala which he lived were nine hundred and sixty-nine years, and he died.” By careful reckoning he is said to have lived fourteen years after the flood. For when he was a hundred and eighty-three years old he begot Lamech; again, Lamech, when he was a hundred and eighty-two years old, begot Noe; and there are three hundred and fifty-five years from Mathusala to the day of Noe’s birth. But the flood came in the six hundredth year of Noe’s life, that is, in the nine hundred and fifty-fifth year of Mathusala; and since he is said above to have lived nine hundred and sixty-nine years, it is plain that he lived fourteen years after the flood. But only eight souls were saved in the ark; so there is an error in the number, as in many places. For in the books of the Hebrews and the Samaritans I found it thus: “And Mathusala lived a hundred and eighty-seven years and begot Lamech; and Mathusala lived after he begot Lamech seven hundred and eighty-two years and begot sons and daughters; and all the days of Mathusala were nine hundred and sixty-nine years, and he died. And Lamech lived a hundred and eighty-two years and begot Noe.” That makes three hundred and sixty-nine years; add to these the six hundred years of Noe, because the flood came in the six hundredth year of his life; and so it comes about that Mathusala died in the nine hundred and sixty-ninth year of his life, namely in the year in which the flood began.
03_interl471: rest, that is, Christ, in whom we find rest
03_marg402: And Noe, etc. JEROME. Noe is interpreted “rest,” because under him all the works of the past came to rest through the flood.
03_marg403: JEROME. The Hebrew word Elohim is of both numbers, for it signifies God and gods. Therefore Aquila dared to say “sons of the gods,” understanding holy gods or angels; following whom Symmachus says: “the sons of the mighty, seeing the daughters of men.”
03_marg404: The sons of God seeing, etc. By the sons of God are understood the godly sons of Seth, who, overcome by desire, took wives from the daughters of men, that is, from the stock of Cain, and begot mighty men, namely huge in body, proud in strength, lawless in ways, who are called giants. It is not unbelievable that such men were begotten by men, not by angels or certain demons who are wanton toward women, because after the flood too the bodies not only of men but also of women were of unbelievable size.
03_interl477: until the flood, for doing penance; during which the ark was built
03_interl478: before the ark began to be made
03_marg405: My spirit shall not remain, etc. JEROME. The Hebrew: “My spirit shall not judge men for ever, because they are flesh”; that is, because the condition of men is frail, I will not keep them for eternal torment, but will pay them here what they deserve. So it is mercy, not severity, that the sinner is visited here for his crime. Whence God, angered, says: “I will not punish your daughters when they shall commit fornication.” And elsewhere: “I will visit their iniquities with a rod,” etc. But lest he seem cruel because he gave no room for penance, he adds: “But his days shall be a hundred and twenty years.” For these are not understood to be the years of human life foretold, since men are found afterwards to have lived longer; but it is understood that God said this to Noe twenty years before the ark began to be made, which is read to have been made in a hundred years, foretelling the flood; not prescribing the span of human life thereafter, but of those whom he was going to destroy by the flood.
03_marg406: And his days shall be, etc. STRABO. Before the flood, namely for doing penance. But because they persevered in malice, they were destroyed before the fixed term, in the hundredth year.
03_interl479: huge in body, proud in strength, lawless in ways; whence giants, that is, sons of the earth, are named
03_marg407: And God seeing, etc. Repentance or sorrow of heart does not befall God, whose judgment of all things is as fixed as his foreknowledge is sure; but Scripture uses everyday words, fitting itself to our littleness, so that from known things we may know the unknown. For the anger of God is not a disturbance of mind but the judgment that is brought on the sinner; and the thought of his heart is the unchangeable reason of things to be changed.
03_interl481: Scripture speaks to us in everyday words, so as to go on from the known to the unknown
03_marg408: GREGORY. In the Morals, book 5. Often in sacred speech the wise draw God’s counsel from the wise of the world. So now, for man’s profit, the very maker of men takes upon himself the voice of human feeling, since it is agreed that he who sees all things before they come made nothing which he should come to his senses about by repenting. So as it is no wonder if spiritual men often use the words of the fleshly, so neither is it to be wondered at if the Creator of all himself, to draw the flesh to understanding him, keeps or takes up in himself the speech of the flesh.
03_interl483: He seems to repent when he changes his work, while his will and disposing remain unmoved.
03_interl484: a traveller, not one who has arrived
03_interl485: that is, according to the perfect justice of the present life, not of the life to come
03_marg409: ALLEGORICALLY. This man by his deeds signifies Christ, who says: “Learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart.” He alone is found just, to whom for his justice seven persons are given; Christ too is just and perfect, to whom seven churches, enlightened by the sevenfold Spirit, are given in one Church. Noe is freed through water and wood, and his household; so the household of Christ through baptism and the cross.
03_marg410: Noe was a just man, etc. If no one is without sin, how was he perfect? Some are called perfect, not as they are to be perfected when they will be made equal to the angels, but as they can be in pilgrimage. Whence he adds: “in his generations,” that is, as he could be perfect by God’s grace after his own measure, not as in the other life, in which he will neither will nor be able to sin. “He walked with God,” following his footsteps.
03_marg411: “In his generations”: as if not of finished justice, but according to his generation.
03_interl490: man, for whose sake all things were created; when he sins, all things are said to be corrupted
03_interl492: of all mortals, except those who were to be saved in the ark as the seed-bed of a second origin
03_interl493: by a judgment well pleasing to me
03_interl494: that is, the dwellers on the earth
03_interl496: so that it should not be fruitful in its own manner
03_marg412: The doctors teach that the greenness and fruitfulness of the earth were far less after the flood, and that therefore the eating of flesh was granted to men, whereas before they lived only on the fruits of the earth.
03_interl500: smoothed, so that nothing harmful should cling to them
03_interl501: because the life of the saints is firm and stable
03_interl503: which is a most fiery glue; timbers smeared with it are loosened by no violence
03_interl505: so that it is not loosened by those who are within or by those who are without
03_marg413: Make thee an ark of timber: namely strong and not to be loosened and well fitted together, which another translation calls “squared,” so that it should be loosened neither by the force of the winds nor by the flood.
03_marg414: Little rooms, etc. STRABO. The SEVENTY: “Thou shalt make it with two storeys and three storeys in the ark”: two storeys in the lower parts, three storeys in the upper; so it was divided into five rooms. The first, that is, the lowest, was for dung, to which the dung flowed down, so that those who were in the ark should not be hurt by the stench. The second was the storeroom. The third, of the fierce animals and serpents. The fourth, of the tame. The fifth, that is, the highest, of men and birds; where the two-storeyed and three-storeyed parts were joined, that is, between the storeroom and the dwelling of the beasts.
03_marg415: In the first dwelling, in the lower parts, the ark had one storey; in the second, above the lower dwelling, two storeys; but in the third, above the second, three storeys.
03_marg416: Others say that in the lower parts there were two little rooms, and so the ark was two-storeyed; of these the lower received the dung, the second the food, which was called the storeroom. In the upper parts it was three-storeyed, where men and animals were kept with fitting distinction.
03_marg417: Noe built the ark of timbers that do not rot, and Christ the Church of men who will live for ever, which, like the ark, floats on the waves. The ark is of squared timbers, the Church of saints, whose stable life is ready for every good work, as a squared timber stands firm on every side. The timbers are glued together with pitch within and without, so that by the fitting-together of unity the patience of charity may be signified, lest the Church, shaken by those who are within or by those who are without, give way from brotherly joining.
03_marg418: For pitch is a most fiery and most strong glue, and signifies the heat of love, bearing all things by the strength of its greatness to hold fellowship together. That the ark is six times as long as it is broad and ten times as long as it is high shows a likeness to the human body, in which Christ appeared. For the length of the body from the crown to the sole holds six times the breadth, which is from one side to the other, and ten times the height, which is from the back to the belly. That the breadth is spread out to fifty cubits signifies the breadth of the heart, which comes about by spiritual charity. Whence: “The charity of God is poured forth in our hearts by the Holy Ghost.” On the fiftieth day after the resurrection Christ sent the Spirit, by whom he enlarged the hearts of believers. And the length of three hundred cubits holds fifty six times, as all the time of the world stretches through six ages, in which Christ has not ceased to be preached: in five, prophesied; in the sixth, proclaimed in the gospel.
03_interl506: geometrical cubits, each of which is made up of six cubits of a human hand
03_interl507: the ark at its foundation was four-sided, of unequal length and breadth, rising from the corners into an arch until the top was finished in one cubit of length and breadth
03_marg419: Three hundred cubits, etc. ISIDORE. In the three hundred cubits the wood of the cross can be shown; for the letter tau, of this number, shows the sign of the cross, by which, made partners of the passion through baptism, we gain the length of eternal life. The height rises to thirty cubits, which number the length holds ten times in three hundred cubits, because Christ is our height, who hallowed the gospel at thirty years, bearing witness that he came not to destroy the law but to fulfil it; and since the law is known in ten commandments, the length of the ark is completed in ten times thirty cubits. Whence too Noe is reckoned tenth from Adam. A hundred, the solid square, made by multiplying ten by itself, signifies the elect who are to be glorified through the justification of the commandments. Whence the man who had a hundred sheep, when one was lost, left the ninety-nine and sought the one that had perished, and when he found it put it back, to make up the hundred; which, multiplied by three, receives the grace of immortality from the Father through the Son and the Holy Spirit, among those who are increased by the grace of the Trinity and who, fallen from the hundred, are made up again to it through knowledge of the Trinity. The breadth of fifty cubits signifies remission, because the fiftieth year, that is, the jubilee, freed slaves, restored possessions, gave pardon to debtors and their homeland to exiles. So Christ in his Church set the number fifty in the breadth; for had he not given the remission of sins, the Church would not have been spread through the world. The number thirty in the height holds a sacrament like that of three hundred. But the whole is brought back to one, because there is one God, of whom are all things, and one faith, and one baptism.
03_marg420: The ark, which was commanded to be made three hundred cubits in length, fifty in breadth, thirty in height, was finished in one cubit. For it signifies the Church, which is broad below and narrow above; because, narrowed a little from the breadth which it still has in its weak members, and advancing on high, it tends to one. For reason requires that within the length of the ark all the beasts, four-footed and creeping things, should have been in the lower parts; man and the flying things in the upper. Near the upper part there was a window in the side, from which the man let out the dove or the raven. So man and the flying things were near the one cubit. For in her many fleshly ones the Church is broad, in her few spiritual ones narrow; and because she is gathered to the one Man who is without sin, she is as it were finished in one cubit. We see many in the Church who are proud, wanton, gaping after earthly things, angry and quarrelsome, and hurting their neighbours. But because the Church bears with them, that they may be converted, they are said, as it were, to have been beasts in the breadth of the ark. We see others who do not seize what belongs to others, bear injury done to them calmly, are content with their own things, and live humbly. But because these are now few, the ark is narrowed. We see others too leaving what they possess, giving no care to earthly things, loving their enemies, taming the flesh, pressing down all movements by reason, raised up on the wing of contemplation by heavenly desire. But because they are very rare, the ark is now drawn in near the cubit, where men and flying things are held. But because no one is without sin except him who was conceived without sin, the ark is finished in one cubit, because there is one author and redeemer of the Church without sin, to whom and through whom all advance who know themselves sinners.
03_interl508: in the Hebrew: “Thou shalt make a noon for the ark.” Symmachus: “Thou shalt make a daylight for the ark,” that is, a window
03_interl509: for sending out the raven or the dove
03_interl510: the Jews hold that this was of crystal
03_marg421: So the Church, gathered in unity, is raised up and advances. Whence: “He that gathereth not with me, scattereth.”
03_interl511: the door in the side of the ark: the wound in the side of Christ
03_marg422: And the door of the ark thou shalt set, etc. For no one enters the Church except through the sacrament of the remission of sins, which flowed from the opened side.
03_marg423: Lower, middle chambers and third stories, etc. The Seventy: “two-storeyed and three-storeyed.” For from all nations the Church gathers either a twofold multitude, from the circumcision and the uncircumcision, or a threefold one, from the three sons of Noe, by whose offspring the world is filled. And the lower parts of the ark are divided, because in this earthly life there is a diversity of nations; but at the top all are finished in one, because Christ is all and in all.
03_marg424: Fittingly the ark came to a point at the top like a sort of narrow roof, so as to shed the threats of the rains; and standing below in the waters with four-square stability, it could be neither tipped over nor sunk by the push of the winds or the onrush of the waves or the restlessness of the animals within.
03_marg425: The ark was broad in the lower parts, narrow in the upper, and at the top it rose to the measure of one cubit. For below it is believed to have held the four-footed beasts and creeping things; above, the birds and men. It is broad where the beasts are, narrow where the men are, because it is broad in the fleshly, narrow in the spiritual. For where it bears with the beastly, it loosens its bosom more widely; where it holds the rational, it is drawn to the top. “For wide is the way that leadeth to destruction, and many there are who go in thereat. Narrow is the gate that leadeth to life, and few there are that find it.” The ark narrows at the top to one cubit, because in the Church, the holier they are, the fewer they are, who are led at the top to him who alone was born a man holy beyond compare, as “a sparrow all alone on the housetop.” So the evil are to be borne with all the more as they are the more numerous; for in the threshing of the floor the grains that are kept in the barns are few, the heaps of chaff that are burnt in the fire great.
03_marg426: Morally, he who turns himself from love of the world builds the ark of salvation in his heart, having in himself length, that is, faith in the Trinity and length of life and immortality; breadth, in charity, by which he can do good even to enemies; height, in hope, by which he lifts himself to heavenly things and refers the sum of his actions to one.
03_interl513: concerning you and your household, to be kept for the restoring of the human race
03_marg427: And of every living creature, etc. AUGUSTINE. It is asked about the tiniest animals, such as mice and lizards, and flies and beetles and fleas, whether the number was kept. But those which are not begotten by mating but are born from the moisture of the earth, or from the corruption of carcasses or other things, did not need to be in the ark; which is hinted when it is said of the birds “according to their kind” and of the beasts “in their kind.” Those too which live in houses, like fleas, mice and flies, did not need to be there by number, since they are understood to have been in the houses in greater numbers then. And those which are born from the mixing of different kinds, like mules, hinnies and the like, are not to be said to have been in the ark. But those which live both in the waters and on land, like otters and seals, had little places prepared outside the ark, in which they could take refuge as on dry land. The same is to be thought of sea and river birds. That all kinds of animals are shut in the ark signifies that the Church is gathered from all peoples and nations; as in Peter’s dish there are clean and unclean animals, so in the sacraments of the Church good and bad are found.
03_interl514: of their own accord; not by the act of man but at the nod of God
03_interl515: so that they should not perish by the flood
03_interl516: as if he were asking whence he should live
03_marg428: Thou shalt take, etc. It is often asked, about the animals which are thought to feed only on flesh, whether they were there beyond the number without breaking the command, because the need of feeding the others had forced them to be shut in; or, as is rather to be believed, whether there could have been foods besides flesh suitable for all. For many animals whose food is flesh feed on fruits and apples, above all the fig and chestnuts. So a just and wise man, warned by God, could find and store up food besides flesh suitable for each; and hunger forces all to eat; and there is nothing that God cannot make pleasant and wholesome, who could even grant by divine power that they should live without food.
03_interl517: so that there should be more that would profit men than that would harm them
03_interl518: all things are clean by nature, but some are called unclean by comparison with a better nature; as the ox is better than the lion, because more needful to man, for whose sake all things were created
03_marg429: Of all clean beasts take, etc. RABANUS. We should take not seven doubled, that is, fourteen, but only seven. Likewise “two and two” is not four but only two, male and female. And it is to be noted that the clean animals are brought in by an odd number, that is, seven, the unclean by an even one; because an odd number holds out the look of virtue, an even one weakness. The clean are more, so that Noe, going out of the ark, should have something to sacrifice and to eat.
03_marg430: “Of all clean beasts take,” etc. Not that the good are more than the evil, but because the good keep the unity of the spirit in the bond of peace, which is commended by a sevenfold working: of wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, godliness and the fear of the Lord. Whence the number fifty, which belongs to the coming of the Holy Spirit, is completed in seven sevens, which are forty-nine, one being added. Whence: “Careful to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.” But the evil are held in two, as being divisible and easy to schism. And Noe with his own is counted eighth, because in Christ the hope of resurrection appeared, who rose on the eighth day, that is, after the seventh of the sabbath; which day, the third from the passion, is both the first and the eighth in the number of the days that roll through all time.
03_marg431: It is asked whether so great an ark could be built in a hundred years by four men, that is, Noe and his three sons. But if it could not, it was no great matter to bring in other craftsmen; who, having received the wages of their work, did not care whether Noe acted wisely or foolishly, and did not enter it, because they did not believe what he believed.
03_interl519: he often repeats the wickedness of the evil by rebuking it, and announces evils to come, so as at least thus to move them to penance
03_marg432: I will rain, etc. ISIDORE. Because all guilt is committed against the ten commandments throughout the whole world, which is divided into four parts; and four tens make forty: whether the guilt is contracted from prosperity, which belongs to the days, or from adversity, which belongs to the nights, it is washed away in baptism.
03_marg433: And he was six hundred years old, etc. ISIDORE. Noe was five hundred years old when the Lord commanded him to make the ark, and six hundred when he had now gone in. From which it is gathered that the ark was built over a hundred years. And the hundreds of years signify the single ages of the world. Whence the sixth hundred, from the completion of five hundred to six hundred, signifies the Church being built in the making known of the gospel. So let him who wants life be a squared timber, ready for every good work, and enter the holy building. The second month of the six hundredth year, too, signifies the sixth age; for two months are closed in sixty days. And from six are named sixty, and six hundred, and six thousand, and six hundred thousand, and so on in greater sums, while the number rises by the same step. That the twenty-seventh day is recalled belongs to the squaring of which it was written above. But here it is to be said more openly that the Trinity makes us ready for every good work: by memory, with which we recall God; understanding, with which we know him; and love, with which we love him. For three times three, and these three times, make twenty-seven, which is three squared.
03_interl521: the women apart, because one must abstain in affliction
03_marg434: And Noe went in, etc. “And his wife,” etc. RABANUS. It is to be noted that Noe goes into the ark with his sons apart, and their wives apart. Therefore it is said separately, “Noe went in and his sons,” and there is added separately, “his wife and the wives of his sons.” But they came out men and women together; for so it is written: “Noe went out, and his wife.” For there is “a time to embrace, and a time to be far from embraces.”
03_interl522: at the divine nod, as they were brought to Adam that he might name them
03_marg435: And after … were passed, etc. ISIDORE. Because we are baptized in the hope of the rest to come, which the seventh day signifies, all flesh outside the ark was consumed by the flood; because outside the Church the water of baptism, though it is the same, avails not for salvation but for ruin.
03_interl524: what was fixed beforehand above he carries out in order
03_interl525: Nisan, which the Latins call May
03_interl526: so that they should not flow gently, as usual, but cover the earth with a sudden flood
03_marg436: ALLEGORICALLY. It is to be noted that the waters of the flood overflowed in the six hundredth year, because in the sixth age of the world the sacrament of baptism was first commended; and this on the seventeenth day of the second month, because ten signifies the ten commandments, and seven, because of the sabbath, signifies the seventh rest; and because in the ten commandments the renouncing of vices is seen, whoever is initiated in baptism professes, for the sake of eternal rest, that he renounces all things within himself.
03_marg437: The windows, namely the clouds, which were opened so that unusual and greater rains should pour from them. Cataracts are properly the mouths of the Nile, but are used loosely for all windows.
03_marg438: It is often asked about the ark whether, with so great a capacity as is described, it could bear all the animals that are said to have gone in, and their food. Origen solves this by the geometrical cubit, asserting that it was not said in vain that Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, who loved geometry, and that the geometrical cubit holds as much as six of ours.
03_marg439: Two and two, etc. AUGUSTINE. He commanded above that seven and seven of the clean, two and two of the unclean should be taken. How then does he now say that two and two went in, whether of the clean or of the unclean? But this refers not to the number of the clean and unclean but to male and female. For in all there are two, male and female. But it is to be noted that what is said, “wherein was the breath of life,” is said not only of men but also of cattle; because some want what is written, “he breathed into his face the spirit of life,” to be understood of the Holy Spirit. But some copies have better “the breath of life.”
03_interl527: what man could not do: lest the waters should come in, God pitched it on the outside
03_marg440: Forty days, etc. ALCUIN. The rain flooded by the number forty, which shows the tribulation of penance. After forty days Noe opened the window, signifying that heaven is opened to those who fast. Whence Moses, Elias and the Saviour himself hallowed fasts by the number forty, as needful in the three times: before the law, under the law, under grace.
03_marg441: The water was fifteen cubits higher, etc. If the earth of Mount Olympus (as history tells) could reach into the space of calm air, where it is said that neither clouds are seen nor wind felt, why not the waters too by rising? But the seventh rest is joined with the eighth resurrection. For when the body is given back, the rest of the saints, which is given after this life, does not end; but the whole man, no longer in hope but in reality, renewed in body and spirit with perfect and immortal salvation, is taken up into eternal life. So in the sacrament of our regeneration, that is, baptism, it is a deep mystery that the water rose fifteen cubits above all the height of the mountains. For seven and eight make fifteen. Seven signifies rest, eight resurrection. So this sacrament of resurrection and rest goes beyond all the wisdom of the proud, so that they cannot search out the rest of the resurrection by the height of their knowledge. And because seventy is named from seven and eighty from eight, the two numbers being joined, the water was lifted up for ninety days, commending and confirming the same height of baptism in hallowing the new man to hold rest and the faith of the resurrection.
03_marg442: There are those who think that neither the quality of the earth nor the height of the mountains was before the flood such and so great as it is today.
03_marg443: ALCUIN. Therefore the land animals perished rather than the water ones, because they live from the cursed earth.
03_interl528: after the flooding of forty days
03_interl529: the Holy Spirit, or a wind, by whose blasts the water should go back
03_marg444: And brought, etc. ALCUIN. It can be understood of that Spirit of which it was said, “The Spirit of God moved over the waters”: then he moved so that, the waters being gathered into their place, the earth should appear; now he is brought so that, the waters of the flood being taken away, he should uncover the face of the earth. By the spirit a wind can be understood, according to that saying, “And the stormy wind stood,” namely by whose blasts the water should go back.
03_interl530: it seems that the courses of rivers and streams return through the veins of the earth to the mother deep
03_marg445: And the waters returned, etc. ALCUIN. It seems that all the courses of rivers return through hidden passages to the deep, according to that saying: “Unto the place from whence the rivers come, they return.”
03_marg446: And the ark rested in the … month, etc. ISIDORE. It signifies the sevenfold rest; and because the perfect rest there, the number of the squaring spoken of above is repeated too. For on the twenty-seventh day of the second month the sacrament is commended, and again on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month it is confirmed, when the ark rested; for what is promised in hope is shown in reality.
03_marg447: Whether these things were done after the hundred and fifty days, or all are recalled by way of summing-up which began to be done after the forty days of rain? So that this alone belongs to the hundred and fifty days, that the water was raised up to the mountains themselves, either from the fountains of the deep when the rain had now stopped, or because it stayed at its height with no wind drying it. But the other things that have been said were not all done after the hundred and fifty days, but are recalled which began to be done from the end of the forty days.
03_marg448: It is to be noted that in the tenth month the tops of the mountains appeared, which the waters of the flood had passed by fifteen cubits; because the sacraments of eternal rest and the glory of the resurrection, which the wisdom of the proud did not know, the eminence of the saints understood through the fulfilling of the commandments. Whence: “By thy commandments I have had understanding.” And elsewhere: “Thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them to little ones.”
03_interl531: In the Hebrew: “It went forth going out and returning, until the waters were dried up.”
03_marg449: ISIDORE. That after forty days the raven did not come back, either cut off by the waters or lured by a floating carcass, figures those most foul with the uncleanness of desire, and therefore too intent on the things that are outside in the world, either to be rebaptized or to be led astray and held by those whom baptism, because of the ark, that is, the Church, kills.
03_marg450: It is asked whether the raven died or could live in some way. For if there was land where it could rest, the dove likewise would have found rest. Whence it is guessed that the raven could settle on a carcass, which the dove naturally shuns.
03_marg451: ISIDORE. The dove sent out, and returning when it found no rest, signifies that through the New Testament rest is not promised to the saints in this world; for it was sent out after forty days, by which number the life that is led in the world is marked.
03_marg452: The ark holds the raven and the dove, and the Church the good and the evil. The raven sent out does not return, because the reprobate, clinging to the enticements of the world, perish. The dove came back carrying an olive branch with green leaves in her mouth, because the saints, rejoicing in simplicity, carry the gift of peace in their mouth, saying: “With them that hated peace I was peaceable: when I spoke to them,” etc.
03_marg453: The question is how the dove did not find where to settle, when the tops of the mountains had already been laid bare, according to the order of the telling. Which can be solved by summing-up, so that the things told later are understood to have been done earlier; or rather, they had not yet dried.
03_marg454: Having waited, etc. The dove, sent out after another seven days because of the sevenfold spiritual working, brought back a fruitful shoot of olive, signifying that many baptized outside the Church, if the richness of charity is not lacking, are brought back at a later time into the fellowship of unity in the mouth of the dove, as in the kiss of peace.
03_marg455: ALCUIN. The dove, the foulest bird having been driven out, carries an olive branch to Noe after the flood, because the dove of the Holy Spirit, coming to Christ after baptism, announces peace with a branch of refreshment and light.
03_marg456: And he stayed yet, etc. ISIDORE. The dove, sent out after another seven days and not returning, signifies the end of the world, when rest will be for the saints not in the sacrament of hope, by which the Church is now joined in fellowship as long as that is drunk which flowed from Christ’s side, but in the perfection of salvation, when the kingdom shall be delivered up to God and the Father, so that in that clear contemplation of the truth we may need no ministries.
03_marg457: ISIDORE. “Of the life of Noe,” that is, when six hundred years are completed, the roof of the ark is opened, because when the sixth age of the world is finished the sacrament is revealed. On the twenty-seventh day of the second month the earth is said to be dried, as if the need of baptizing were ended.
03_marg458: STRABO. That is, May. Noe spent a year in the ark and went out on the very day on which he had gone in. For he went in on the seventeenth day of the second month; now it says that he went out on the twenty-seventh day of the same month. But it is to be known that if eleven are added to the present day, as the moon is today, so it will be a year later on that day. So when Noe went in, it was the seventeenth moon, or the seventeenth day of the second month. Therefore after a year, eleven being added, it was the twenty-seventh day and the twenty-seventh moon.
03_marg459: “In the second month,” etc. As was said above, on the seventeenth day of the six hundredth year the earth was soaked by the waters of the flood, but on the twenty-seventh of the second month it was dried, when it was commanded that they should go out of the ark and receive a covenant, that they should no more perish by the waters of a flood. In which it can be understood that by seventeen, as above, the state of beginners can be signified, when vices are renounced; by twenty-seven the advancement of the perfect in the completion of virtues. For if you add ten to seventeen, it makes twenty-seven. For if to the ten commandments, by which sin is renounced, you add the perfection of the gospel, by which it is commanded not only not to be angry but even to love enemies and the like, you have come to that age of perfection in which you need not the sacraments spoken of; and going out of the ark, that is, coming from hope to hope, you will find the rest promised in the sacraments.
03_interl532: the men and women go out together who went in apart
03_marg460: Go out of the ark, etc. ISIDORE. They go out joined who went in apart, because now the flesh lusteth against the spirit and the spirit against the flesh; but in the resurrection of the just the body will cling to the spirit in perfect peace, with no need or desire of changeableness resisting.
03_interl533: because the world was to be filled by these, the blessing of the first creation is given back
03_marg461: And taking, etc. AUGUSTINE. Clean and unclean animals went into the ark, but after the going out only the clean are offered to God. But what he says, “I will not strike every living soul as I have done,” and what he adds, which goodness gives the unworthy by its bounty, perhaps figures the indulgence of the New Testament; so that the past vengeance belongs to the severity of the law, this to the goodness of grace.
03_marg462: For the imagination, etc. GREGORY. In the Morals, book 38. Let no one ascribe it to himself if he has overcome his thoughts; because the evil of corruption which each has taken from the rise of fleshly desires works on as age advances, and unless the hand of divine strength quickly checks it, fault swallows up all the good of nature into the deep. “Neither he that planteth is any thing, nor he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase.”
03_marg463: Man is set over the other animals in the inner man, as a comfort after the vengeance that had been carried out, and lest a few men be overwhelmed by many beasts; and that they may know that they rule over the irrational, not over the rational.
03_interl536: man is set over not men but the irrational
03_marg464: GREGORY. Man by nature was set over not the rational but the irrational. Therefore it is said to him that he should be feared by the animals, not by man; because it is against nature to be proud and to wish to be feared by an equal. Whence the ancient fathers are said to have been not kings of men but shepherds of flocks. So nature brought forth all men equal; but for various merits God’s just but hidden dispensing sets some over others, so that those who do not fear the divine judgments may be afraid to sin through fear of men. But let those set over others not be proud of this fear, in which they should seek not their own glory but the justice of those under them. For they rule not over men but over beasts, because in the part in which they are beastly they are subjected to fear. So the swelling of pride is to be pressed down by the hand of the humblest consideration. For if the mind comes down within itself from the summit of its height, it will find the plain of natural equality, so as to rejoice not in being over others but in doing them good.
03_interl538: because the seat of the soul is in the blood
03_marg465: ISIDORE. All animals are given them for food, because in the calling of the Gentiles to the faith there is no difference, which is figured in Peter’s dish. They are forbidden to eat blood, so that the former life should not be held in the conscience as if choked, but poured out through confession. The eating of flesh seems to have been granted after the flood because of the barrenness of the earth and the frailty of man.
03_interl540: he wants every man to be understood as the brother of every man, because all are from one
03_marg466: Behold I will establish, etc. God set a testament between himself and men and every living soul, that he would not destroy it by a flood: namely the bow which appears in the clouds, which never shines except from the sun. For they do not perish by the flood, cut off from the Church, who in the prophets and in all the holy Scriptures, as in God’s clouds, recognise the glory of Christ and do not seek their own. But lest worshippers of this sun swell up, let them know that Christ is signified by the sun as by a lion, by a lamb, by a stone: for the sake of likeness, not by the property of substance.
03_marg467: I will set my bow, etc. ALCUIN. God gave the bow as a sign of safety, lest fearful men, often seeing floods of rain, should fear to be destroyed by another flood. It was set in heaven so that it could be seen by all, and that in any tribulation we should lift up the eyes of the heart to him who dwells in heaven. And because the bow does not come except from the rays of the sun and a moist cloud, it seems that there had been no rains before the flood; but the earth could be made fruitful by dew and the overflowing of springs.
03_marg468: The bow has two colours, sky-blue and fiery, which express two judgments: one of water, which is past; the other of fire, which is believed to be coming at the end of the world. Whence the sky-blue colour is on the outside, the fiery on the inside.
03_interl541: by the sky-blue colour marking the past flood, by the fiery the judgment to come
03_marg469: JEROME. Often the Seventy, not being able to turn into Greek the letter heth, which sounds a double aspiration, added the Greek chi, teaching that in such words there is to be aspiration. Whence they rendered Cham for what is Ham, from whom Egypt is called Ham in the Egyptians’ tongue to this day.
03_interl547: the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel
03_interl548: with the cup of the passion
03_interl550: he was crucified, where the weakness of mortality appeared
03_interl551: others: in his house, that is, in his own nation, namely the Jewish
03_marg470: Christ too was made drunk when he suffered, uncovered when he was crucified. “In his tent,” that is, among the household of his own blood; then the mortality of the flesh was laid bare: to the Jews a stumbling-block, to the Gentiles foolishness; but to them that are called, Jews and Gentiles, as Sem and Japheth, the power of God and the wisdom of God; because “the foolishness of God is wiser than men.”
03_marg471: After the flood Noe was made drunk, because perhaps he did not know that one could be made drunk by wine; for before the flood men are not read to have used wine. Therefore it is said of Noe specially that he planted a vineyard. The uncovering of the thigh follows drunkenness, as lust follows fullness.
03_interl552: because he consented to the killing of Christ
03_interl554: the middle brother, that is, the people of the Jews, which neither held the first place of the apostles nor believed last among the Gentiles
03_interl556: through the letter of the law and of prophecy
03_marg472: Which when … had seen, etc. ISIDORE. The Jews, seeing the death of Christ, mocked it. But Sem and Japheth, the two peoples believing from the uncircumcision and the circumcision, covered it turned away and did not see. We cover the passion of Christ with a kind of veil, that is, we honour it by a sacrament, and, giving the reason of its mystery, we cover it from the detraction of the Jews. For the garment signifies the sacrament, the backs the memory of things past; for the passion is past, not looked for as to come. Cham saw, because he consented to the Lord’s death. He told it outside, because through him was made plain what was secret in the prophet. Therefore he is made a servant of the servants of his brethren, because that nation, as the Christians’ book-bearer, carries the law and the prophets in witness for the Church, so that we may honour by a sacrament what that letter announces.
03_marg473: Which when, etc. Heretics are reckoned in the cursed middle, because they are recognised neither in the wall which believed from the circumcision, from which the apostles came, nor in that from the uncircumcision, from which the Gentiles run together into the unity of faith as into the peace of the corner.
03_interl557: the two sons, the eldest and the youngest, are the two peoples
03_interl558: the sacrament of the passion that is past
03_interl559: honouring with a veil that from which they know they were born
03_interl560: because they did not consent to the killing of Christ
03_marg474: But Sem, etc. GREGORY. In the Morals. We are said to turn away from what we disapprove. What then is it that the sons, coming turned away, covered their father’s nakedness with cloaks thrown over their backs, unless that the good under authority so dislike the evils of those set over them that they hide them from others? Turned away, they bring the covering, because, judging the deed and revering the master, they will not see what they cover.
03_interl562: the Jewish people, which, when it crucified Christ, passed the punishment on to its children, saying: “His blood be upon us and upon our children”
03_marg475: GREGORY. In the Morals, book 26. God does not let many sins go before, but begins his judgment in our correction so that it may come to rest in the damnation of the reprobate. For “judgment begins at the house of God.” What then is the end of those who have not believed, who do not feel temporal scourges because they will perish for ever? Whose wickedness was figured in Cham’s sinning, to whom it is said: “Cursed be Chanaan the boy,” etc. When the father sinned, the son received the sentence, because the wickedness of the reprobate prospers long here but perishes afterwards.
03_marg476: Though God is the God of all nations, as by a proper name he is called the God of Israel even among the nations themselves; which comes from the blessing of Japheth, because among the people of the Gentiles the Church has taken the whole world; which was foretold when it was said, “May God enlarge Japheth.”
03_marg477: STRABO. From whom the Chanaanites, who by this curse are foretold to be driven out of the place of their dwelling.
03_interl565: the Jews and Gentiles coming together in the Church
03_interl566: in the Churches which the apostles, the sons of the prophets, built
03_interl567: the keeper of the books of God
03_marg478: May God enlarge Japheth, etc. JEROME. From Sem the Hebrews, from Japheth the Gentiles. So because the multitude of believers is broad, he is named from the breadth which is called Japheth. But what he says, “and may he dwell in the tents of Sem,” is prophesied of us, who, Israel being cast out, are busied in the learning and knowledge of the Scriptures.
03_marg479: ISIDORE. “May God enlarge,” etc. Sem, the elder by birth, is the Jewish people, from whom are the patriarchs and prophets and apostles. Japheth is the father of the Gentiles, who is interpreted “breadth.” For the Gentile people has been spread wide, which receives the inheritance with the prophets and apostles. And the dwelling of Japheth passed into the tents of Sem, that is, the Church is justified in the house of the law and the prophets. For it is lesser in age of time, but greater by the law of grace. But Cham, which is interpreted “crafty,” is as it were the middle one, set apart from both, neither among the firstfruits of the Israelites nor in the fullness of the Gentiles. He signifies not only the Jews but also crafty heretics, not with the spirit of wisdom but of impatience, with which they are wont to burn first and to trouble the saints. He signifies also all false Christians, who proclaim the passion of Christ by professing it but dishonour it by living badly: “By their fruits you shall know them.” He is cursed not in himself but in his son, as in his fruit, that is, in his work; for Chanaan is interpreted “their movement,” that is, their work.
